questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Australian culture and the opportunity to travel around in Australia and New Zealand.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Loved it! Best half year with so many new fun experiences, travels and friends. Can only recommend going on exchange and Melbourne was such a great city. It had everything - bars, restaurant, vintage stores, cafes, museum, parks and st kilda beach. Fell in love with.  University of Melbourne is very pretty (oxford style) and lots of different subjects to choose from. (Although I used very little time on studying and spent most traveling around),

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Stop 1 is a great help and it was easy to change subject (until 2 weeks after orientation). However be aware that the classes with the best schedule fills up quickly.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was some obligatory orientation the first day (went to that) where you some general information. There is a whole orientation week, but the weather was bad in Melbourne (arrived in June), so went on a trip instead, before the semester started. Don't think you need to go orientation week, as you can look information up online or call stop 1.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: A girl in the KU facebook group posted that she had contact to a rental apartment in Fitzroy, so ended up living with her and another girl. I was very lucky as most people on exchange had to use some time when we arrived on finding a place to stay. If you have not found anything before coming I also got recommend booking The Nunnery hostel in Melbourne, as a lot of other student live there the first two weeks, while looking for apartments. Maybe you can team up with other students. Also the facebook group fairy floss is also very popular for finding housing (maybe you can even get to live with Australians!).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Less expensive (as you only pay for the months you actually live there and not a full half year). However more difficult to find.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Uni housing is very expensive.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Showed up first day with my passport.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Stop 1 student help center.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Most subject where available, but the making the schedule go up can be difficult if the different class times don't line up.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look into subjects before you go, but know that you can change after you get there.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
My two economics subject (Environmental economics and International Macroeconomics) where teacher at same difficulty level as in KU (maybe a little easier), but they curve the grading so even though the final exam wasn't the easiest, we all ended up with good grades. The two business subjects (Consulting Fundamentals and Management competencies) were very easy and I only really took them so I didn't have to go to a final exam.

If you are looking for an easy semester don't take actual ECON subjects as these all have obligatory final exams. Many of the business subjects don't have hurdle requirements so if you score enough points during the semester you don't have to go to the final exam.
Bu honestly don't be worried about failing or the level being to difficult - if you can take the subject at KU you can definitely take and pass with ease in UniMelb.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
ECON subejcts - BA level
Business subjects - MA level 

But ECON subjects are more difficult (weirdly enough).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
ECON subjects follow the same style with a lecture (2 hours) and then a tutorial (1 hour).

Business subjects are "seminar" style with 30-40 people (3 hours) and more interactive, as the teacher asks questions and participation is sometimes part of the grade. Also, they included a lot of group work... which sometimes was good and sometimes was bit of a pain.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Environmental economics, International Macroeconomics, Consulting Fundamentals and Management competencies

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Depends on what type of semester you are looking for. 

I liked that Environmental economics included an essay as sometimes KU subjects lacks assignments which practices conveying and writing about economic issues and solutions. The exam and other assignments reminded me a lot of Microeconomics 2. Quotas vs. tax, tragedy of the commons and so on. International macroeconomics is about different models to determine the current account, trade balance, interest rate and so on. I liked it and if you like Macroeconomics 3 or similar subjects at KU, you will like this subjects.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
I spend a lot of money on traveling during and after the semester, but this was also a priority for me. 

In regards to food: UniMelb has a free frozen meal and fresh food program which saved me some money. Great cheap options for those days where you just need something quick, cheap and easy.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is as expensive as in Denmark. Wine is cheap, all other alcohol is more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a surf club, but it was impossible to get on their tours. There was also a mountaineering club, which seemed nice, but I didn't up going on any of their trips.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Fitness, swimming, dance, etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I know some who took dance classes through uni and like it a lot.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go travel! Both in Victoria but also in other states. 

If you have time I can also really recommend New Zealand and Fiji.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Everyone speaks english so easy to integrate.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: In my business subject there were almost only students from asia, who didn't always have the best english speaking abilities. This did make group work a bit more difficult, but it ended up working out.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I loved the city! Especially Fitzroy (a lot like Nørrebro), and all the things you are able to do there and the rest of Melbourne.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Have fun and enjoy it! Although the process is difficult ( a lot of practical stuff around exchange) it is so so worth it!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Use the revolut app as an extra card.
Us All trails to find hikes.
Use campermate to find campgrounds, water, toilets, and so on, if you choose to go in a caravan

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Traveling! Seeing different parts of Australia, surfing, scuba diving, hiking!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: A lot of things going on all the time - remember to also take breaks.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
